title: Verifier-Guided Adaptive Task Decomposition for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
research_question: Can a verifier-guided controller that dynamically revises task decomposition during execution reduce failure cascades and token cost compared with static multi-agent workflows on complex reasoning tasks?
hypothesis: Static decompositions cause avoidable downstream errors when early subtasks are underspecified or incorrect; inserting a verifier that monitors intermediate artifacts and triggers selective re-decomposition will improve end-task accuracy and efficiency over fixed-plan orchestration.
motivation: The knowledge base shows recent rejected ideas concentrated on uncertainty averaging and escalation policies for agent orchestration, suggesting a saturation point around risk scoring alone but leaving a gap on structural adaptation of the workflow itself. Separately, the self-adaptive systems evidence highlights that overcommitting to a single model or plan can produce poor predictions and unnecessary adaptations, motivating transfer of adaptive feedback-loop ideas to agent workflows. A promising new direction is to treat task decomposition as a revisable object rather than a one-shot plan: a verifier monitors intermediate outputs, detects likely decomposition mismatch, and selectively re-plans only the failing branch. This targets a practical weakness of current multi-agent systems—failure propagation from early bad decompositions—while avoiding overlap with already rejected uncertainty-averaging proposals.
